title: CS2 World Bundle lights (lights.json, contract section 7.2)
description: A flat object whose values are arrays of light entries. ONE FILE, TWO RECORD SHAPES, and they are keyed differently and placed by opposite rules — a consumer that treats them uniformly makes every light or none. PROCEDURAL entries (no 'kind') are emissive-material behaviours keyed by SUB-MESH assetId (the glTF node name inside the owning prefab's .glb) and carry no position, because the light IS the material: place each at the centroid of the primitive using that material slot. PUNCTUAL entries ('kind': 'punctual') are HDRP lights on EffectPrefab entities keyed by the OBJECT prefab's assetId (joining instances.jsonl and meshes/) and DO carry a position — use it, do not fall back to the centroid rule, which would move every streetlamp to the middle of its pole. On the reference city: 1,878 procedural slots against 654 punctual lights, over 1,186 keys, and no key mixes the two.

slot.description: Procedural only. Index into the owning sub-mesh's ProceduralLight buffer, and the join to the geometry: the emitter belongs wherever the primitive using the corresponding material slot is. This is the whole of its placement — inventing a transform here would be inventing data.

materialId.description: Procedural only, and the game's own join. EmissiveProperties.SingleLightMapping.materialId — the owning sub-mesh's MATERIAL SLOT, which is the position of the primitive using it in the same .glb (MeshRipSystem writes one primitive per MeshMaterial entry, in buffer order). Present since 2026-08-19; an entry without it is from an older rip, and a consumer falls back to matching a mesh's slots against its emissive materials in primitive order — exact on 81.8 % of the reference city's slot-carrying meshes and a guess on the rest. Mutually exclusive with layerId.

layerId.description: Procedural only. EmissiveProperties.MultiLightMapping.layerId — this entry drives a material LAYER rather than one material, and the bundle has no layer concept, so a mesh-material consumer skips it and counts it. The multi lights come FIRST in the ProceduralLight buffer, so a low 'slot' may carry either id. Mutually exclusive with materialId.

color.description: The light's authored colour, linear RGBA. On a procedural entry this is the LIT colour; on a punctual entry it is the authored LightEffect colour before photometry.

colorOff.description: Procedural only. The UNLIT colour. 'responseSpeed' is how fast the emitter crosses between the two, which is what makes a day/night cycle look right rather than switching.

purpose.description: Procedural only. CS2's ProceduralLight.m_Purpose name, verbatim — 'NeonSign', 'TrafficLight_Red', 'BrakeLight', 'Headlight_LowBeam', … 47 distinct values on the reference city. An OPEN game enum: match what you know and ignore the rest.

responseSpeed.description: Procedural only. How fast the emitter crosses between 'color' and 'colorOff'.

animation.description: Procedural only. ProceduralLight.m_AnimationIndex, emitted only when >= 0 (an absent key means no animation). Which curve the game drives the emitter's blink or sweep with; the curves themselves are not exported.

kind.description: Present, and only ever 'punctual', on a real HDRP light. Its absence is what marks a procedural entry.

effect.description: Punctual only. Name of the EffectPrefab this light came from.

position.description: Punctual only. Position in metres IN THE OBJECT FRAME — not relative to any sub-mesh. (Corrected 2026-08-14: this said 'relative to the sub-mesh named by parentMesh when >= 0'. A sweep of every reader of Effect.m_ParentMesh finds three, and not one of them places the light: EffectTransformSystem uses it for COLOUR only, SubObjectSystem for sub-object elevation flags, BuildingInitializeSystem for fire SFX. The light's transform comes from GetEffectTransform, which branches on m_BoneIndex — see 'boneIndex'.) Bundle frame axes (section 2.1); NOT mesh-frame converted, so do not negate x.

rotation.description: Punctual only. Rotation as a unit quaternion [x, y, z, w], same frame as 'position'.

parentMesh.description: Punctual only. WHICH SUB-MESH'S COLOUR THIS LIGHT TAKES, not where it sits: it pairs with 'colorChannel', and EffectTransformSystem reads it only as an index into the owner's MeshColor buffer (guarded by parentMesh >= 0 and buffer length). It is EffectSource.m_ParentMesh verbatim and is OVERLOADED across the game's other uses, so it is not a plain index: 0 is by far the commonest value, -1 means none, a value > 0 that exceeds the prefab's sub-mesh count is a ProceduralBone CONNECTION ID (RenderingUtils.FindBoneIndex), and other negatives are authored values the game itself cannot resolve (-1001 occurs on a modded asset in the reference city; FindBoneIndex requires boneID > 0, so the game falls back to the object frame). Do not index a sub-mesh array with it without bounds-checking.

boneIndex.description: Punctual only, and present ONLY when the light rides an animated procedural bone (Effect.m_BoneIndex.x >= 0, resolved by the game at prefab initialise). ITS PRESENCE CHANGES WHAT 'position' MEANS: FindBoneIndex transforms position and rotation into that bone's bind-pose space, so an entry carrying this key is NOT in the object frame and a consumer placing it there puts the light in the wrong spot. [boneIndex, subMesh]: the first is the index into the owner's BoneHistory buffer (an animation the bundle does not carry), the second the sub-mesh whose transform is applied after it, or -1. A static consumer either composes the bind pose or skips these; on the reference city at most 4 of 654 punctual lights can take one — the three bicycles and one park asset whose parentMesh exceeds their prefab's sub-mesh count.

range.description: Punctual only. LightEffectData.m_Range in metres — how far the light reaches, which is what the game culls on.

intensityScale.description: Punctual only. Per-placement multiplier on the prefab's intensity. Emitted only when it differs from 1.

finalColor.description: Punctual only. The RESOLVED colour the renderer is handed: authored colour x photometric intensity x temperature x dimmer, linear HDR (so components may exceed 1). Prefer this over recomputing from 'color' + 'intensity' + 'temperature'.

colorChannel.description: Punctual only. When present, this light takes the OWNING INSTANCE's colorSet channel (0, 1 or 2) instead of its authored colour — the game swaps it in per instance, so a consumer baking 'finalColor' into every copy gets one colour where the city shows several.

type.description: Punctual only. Game.Rendering.LightType name — 'Point', 'Spot', 'Directional', 'Area'. Open; only Point and Spot occur on the reference city.

intensity.description: Punctual only. Photometric intensity in the unit named by 'intensityUnit'.

intensityUnit.description: Punctual only. HDRP LightUnit name — 'Lux', 'Lumen', 'Candela', 'Nits', 'Ev100'. Open, and it is NOT constant across bundles: the reference city reads 'Lux' throughout while contract section 7.2's worked example shows 'Lumen'. Convert; do not assume.

temperature.description: Punctual only. Colour temperature in kelvin, emitted only when the light actually uses one (m_UseColorTemperature). Absent means the authored colour stands alone.

spotShape.description: Punctual, Spot only. HDRP SpotLightShape name ('Cone', 'Pyramid', 'Box').

spotAngle.description: Punctual, Spot only. Outer cone angle in degrees.

innerSpotPercentage.description: Punctual, Spot only. Where the falloff starts, as a percentage of the outer angle.

areaShape.description: Punctual, Area only. HDRP AreaLightShape name ('Rectangle', 'Tube', 'Disc').
